nodes.label: The Three Processes (Producer / Consumer / Aggregator)
nodes.rationale: The two consumers absorb a redelivery by completely different means because only one can get away with the easy one: persisting a trade twice stores the same row, folding a trade into a bar twice adds its size twice. An accumulating consumer must record how far it has applied each partition, in the same transaction as its output.

nodes.label: Kafka Topology as Built
nodes.rationale: Four topics exist and all four are used; the five specified for later phases are not created because a topic with no producer and no consumer is an empty name in a broker. Six partitions is the ceiling on consumer parallelism and is deliberately not 1, because changing the count later repartitions the keyspace and breaks per-symbol ordering in flight.

nodes.label: End-to-End Delivery Semantics
nodes.rationale: Producer idempotence covers retries within one producer session; it does not cover a producer that crashes after the broker wrote the record but before the acknowledgement arrived. The duplicate is expected and absorbed downstream — that is the design, not a gap in it.

nodes.label: Three Layers of Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Deterministic ids, a bounded in-flight window, and database constraints — and the important one is the last, because it is the only guarantee. A redelivered bar is re-upserted with identical values, which rewrites the row and moves updated_at; it is not a no-op, and a test asserts that honestly.

nodes.label: Retryable vs Permanent Classification
nodes.rationale: Confusing the two produces the two worst outcomes available — a poison message that stops a partition forever, or a database outage that silently discards an hour of market data. A permanently rejected batch is replayed one event at a time so one bad row costs one event, not the batch.

nodes.label: One Retry Budget, One Owner
nodes.rationale: TW_CONSUMER_MAX_RETRIES is the processor's storage-attempt budget and nothing else retries. Nesting a retry loop inside another produces a number of attempts nobody can predict from configuration and an outage that lasts far longer than the operator expects.

nodes.label: The Dead-Letter Topic and Its Headers
nodes.rationale: Carries the original bytes verbatim and the original key so partitioning is preserved, plus namespaced reason/source/attempt headers. A failure to write to the DLQ is not swallowed — acknowledging a message that was neither stored nor quarantined would be the one path in this system that loses data silently.

nodes.label: The Two Consumer Groups
nodes.rationale: Independent offsets that cannot affect each other — the fan-out Kafka was chosen for, which Phase 2 had asserted without demonstrating. auto_offset_reset=earliest so a new group processes history rather than silently skipping it; auto-commit is off and must stay off.

nodes.label: MarketDataProcessor (as built)
nodes.rationale: Depends on the MarketDataStore port rather than a repository, which is what lets its batching and failure handling be unit-tested with no database. An unregistered symbol gets a provisional row on first sight, because a symbol appearing mid-stream is normal and dropping its data would produce a gap that looks exactly like a quiet market. discard_pending() was added in Phase 2 because a consumer cannot exit on a poison batch the way a one-shot pipeline could.

nodes.label: API Status Codes Carry Meaning
nodes.rationale: 404 means stop asking; 422 means the request is wrong; 200 with an empty list means there is simply no data, because returning 404 for a market that has not opened makes a normal Sunday indistinguishable from a typo; 503 means retry later rather than 500, which tells a client retrying is pointless.

nodes.label: The Frontend's Four States
nodes.rationale: Loading, error with the API's message and a retry, empty (a known symbol with no data — not an error), and success. Getting these wrong is what makes a data UI feel broken. Recharts was chosen because SVG output can be asserted against in jsdom.

nodes.label: Structured Observability Events and Split Counters
nodes.rationale: Counters sit wherever an event could otherwise have vanished and are split on purpose: 'committed the offset' and 'wrote the row' are different claims, and a bug that makes them disagree is the one worth catching. Never a full payload at error level — a quote book logged per tick is how a disk fills during a volatile open.

nodes.label: Narrow ProducerClient / ConsumerClient Protocols
nodes.rationale: A real broker will not fail on demand, so the adapters declare narrow protocols over the handful of methods they call; a client that refuses to connect or fails to commit is then a few lines of test code rather than an unpluggable network cable.
